newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ refrains from money market operation - traders.
newsitem.headline: BOJ refrains from money market operation - traders.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation on Wednesday, money traders said.

Market participants had expected the central bank to take either a neutral or slightly accommodative stance on Wednesday, which is the first day of the new reserves reporting period, by draining about 100 billion or 200 billion yen.
The money market was in surplus of about 200 billion yen going into the day, traders said.

Following the BOJ's inaction, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.45 percent, down from around 0.48 percent earlier. Tuesday's weighted average of the overnight call rate was 0.42 percent.
